properties.name: Every design available to measure grew organically — ours predate reflow2 having rungs, and the bluesky stack was never designed by SE at all — so nothing in reach can say what a WELL-DECOMPOSED design looks like. flo2 is the only deliberately-shaped one, n=1
properties.statement:
MEASURED AND THEN REFRAMED, 2026-08-25. The question being chased was empirical: how deep should a decomposition go, and what carries depth? Two rounds of measurement were taken and BOTH turn out to answer a different question than the one asked.

ROUND 1 — SEVEN REFLOW2 DESIGNS (flo2, qbench, dynograph-foundation, dev_storyflow x2, mapwright, music_graph, reflow2's own). Anthony's correction: *"most of these are after the fact... they were developed before reflow2 really started defining rungs. they might have been done differently if reflow2 defined rungs when these designs were first started."* CONTAMINATED — evidence of what happens with NO guidance.

ROUND 2 — THE BLUESKY STACK, chosen precisely because nobody here designed it. Measured from public trees: bluesky 42 source modules / top package fan-out 22; ophyd 43 / 24; databroker 59 / 27; event-model 29 / 10; tiled 207 / 28 with 8 packages over seven. Every core repo exceeds the 3–7 span-of-control bound at its top package by 3–4x.

🛑 AND THE READING GIVEN OF THAT MEASUREMENT WAS WRONG, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THIS NODE. It was reported as "the stack obeys the doctrine perfectly at the SYSTEM level — five core repos, inside 3–7, and independent lifecycles draw the same cut, two rules agreeing." Anthony: *"the bluesky stack has grown somewhat organically and iteratively. probably if we'd used systems engineering upfront, it would have been designed differently... it was never designed from a systems engineering perspective"* — offered explicitly as hypothesis, not fact.

⭐ THE CORRECTION IS SHARPER THAN "THAT WAS A COINCIDENCE", AND IT HAS A NAME. **CONWAY'S LAW — rule 3 of the same doctrine — PREDICTS a five-way split without anyone doing systems engineering.** Structure mirrors the communication structure that produced it. So finding a five-repo boundary inside 3–7 is NOT evidence that SE happened; it is equally consistent with the split being organisational and the doctrine merely DESCRIBING what organic growth produces. **Two of the four rules cannot distinguish a designed system from a grown one, because one of them is about growth.**

⇒ THE CONSEQUENCE FOR EVERY MEASUREMENT TAKEN TODAY: an organically-grown system tells you what organic growth produces. It cannot tell you what a well-decomposed design looks like, because no such design is in the sample. **THE EVIDENCE CLASS DOES NOT EXIST YET** — not because it was not looked for, but because designs shaped by SE upfront, with reflow2, have not been built.

⭐⭐ THE ONE EXCEPTION, AND IT IS n=1. **flo2** is the only design measured that was shaped deliberately and EARLY — still in concept phase, 12 components. It is also the only one that satisfies the doctrine on every axis measured: depth 3 (the deepest per-component ratio in the sample), fan-out 6/2/2/1/1 with ZERO parents over seven, and 7 interfaces for 12 components. The smallest and youngest design is the best-decomposed one. That is either the strongest available evidence that shaping early works, or a sample of one — and it is honestly both.

📌 WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE LADDER QUESTION. Anthony: *"that is kind of one of the main goals of reflow2 in doing systems engineering upfront and properly (particularly for users that don't do systems engineering — bluesky stack was a bunch of scientists that made something work, which got it momentum, and then added to, and so on)."* The bluesky stack is not a counter-example to reflow2; **it is the target case.** It is also his real operating context — NSLS-II, a ~10-year-old stack being evolved on the fly — so it belongs in the design as a BROWNFIELD adopt subject, not as an exemplar to imitate.

⚠️ BOUNDS, and they are wide. The bluesky figures are file-tree structure from public GitHub metadata, NOT a design decomposition — and the distinction is the other half of round 2: a Python package holding 22 modules is a namespace managed by tooling, whereas a design node's children are things a person must reason about together, which is what span of control actually bounds. Nothing here was cloned, run, or read beyond public trees. The claim that flo2 is well-decomposed rests on structural measures only; nobody has asked whether its decomposition is USEFUL.
